title: Path selection and an elliptic inequality on degenerating Ricci-flat trees
coverage:
Read all of Sections 1, 2 and 7 in full. From Section 4, read the weight choices (q0, q1, lambda, nu, nu', gamma_g), the DeTurck gauge set-up, Lemma ell:comparison and the definitions of F and J with the bound J <= CM^2. From Section 3, read Definition path:def-admissible, Theorem path:selection, Corollary path:variation, Lemma path:sector-uniqueness, about half of Lemma path:clock, the opening of Proposition path:centers, Lemma path:sign-elimination and the final proof of the path-selection theorem.

Checks I did by hand (all came out consistent):
- Lemma 2.1 (ell:functional) scaling and volume integrals: the child-half bound a_c^2 * integral of e^{(2-mu)tau} <= C a_p^2 (1+L) e^{-min(2+mu,4)L}; convergence of the root quadratic density, r^{1-2q}; the boundary term O(D^{2-2q}); and DE(2g) = 2 * integral of R.
- Root weights: q1 < q0 makes J converge; q0 + q1 > 2 makes the dual pairing for dz converge.
- Lemma ell:differential (the dF estimate): child-side volume factor e^{-8L}, transport collar L^2 norm a_p^2 e^{-2L}, descendant volume a_p^4 e^{-4L}.
- Scalar-volume child bound in Proposition ell:all-orders.
- The contradiction chain: |F| >= eps*M/2 together with J <= CM^2 gives F^2 >= c0*J, then Corollary path:variation gives finite variation of log|F|.
- The harmonic-measure step in Lemma path:sector-uniqueness, the Hermite signature at repeated and complex roots, the sign-indicator polynomials, and the worked example e^{-L1} - L2 e^{-L2} = 0.

Not verified in detail: the long inductive proofs of Lemma path:clock (change of clock), Lemma path:adjoin-p, Proposition path:centers (about 600 lines), Lemma path:prepared-contours and Lemma path:roots; the augmented inverse and seam lemmas of Section 4; and Sections 5-6 (tail calculus and length expansions). Those parts are where a hidden gap would most likely sit.
main_claim: Fix a finite rooted tree of 4D Ricci-flat ALE/orbifold pieces with a root end decaying like r^{-q}, q > 1. Take a sequence of joined metrics whose joining lengths all go to infinity and whose scale-neutral weighted Ricci error M goes to 0. Then the renormalized Einstein-Hilbert functional satisfies E = o(M). The proof rests on a multivariable path-selection theorem for exponential-polynomial asymptotic classes, combined with a Lojasiewicz-type variation argument.
